actualPaths.facts: Parent writes one SGR press with x+1/y+1 and releases only after typed-delivery wait. Original stdin remains the PTY slave. initInput enters raw mode; initInputReader starts ultraviolet before initial View; StreamEvents scans input and sends decoded events. Decoder accepts exactly three SGR parameters, converts one-based coordinates to zero-based and distinguishes M press/m release.
actualPaths.alternatives: Unrecorded partial/failed parent write, unread/incomplete/other decoded input cannot be excluded by output alone. Unix SGR decoding is not proof of enabled physical-terminal reporting.

actualPaths.facts: BubbleTea translates ultraviolet mouse event before fixture filter. Only admitted MouseClick passes safeMouse. Releases/motion/other messages are dropped by current default policy. Accepted raw mouse increments aggregate Update inputs but does not itself inspect; the renderer separately obtains OnMouse.
actualPaths.alternatives: Type/policy/coordinate/frame differences and other input branches need counters; no blanket conclusion that no input arrived follows from produced=0.

actualPaths.facts: p.render calls model.View before renderer.render; fixture publishes progress inside View. Renderer flush is ticker-driven. Tick first flushes Program query output, then renderer.flush. renderer.flush holds its mutex across io.Copy and only afterward assigns lastView. onMouse reads lastView.OnMouse under that same mutex and invokes the copied callback after unlock.
actualPaths.candidate: A query-only parent drain can satisfy the current progress-ready predicate before first renderer commit. A click then can see no committed OnMouse; later output still appears. This ordering is source-consistent, not proven for this failure.

actualPaths.facts: Original mouseHandler captures frame/regions/geometry, returns nil on wrong type/button/out-of-bounds/no region, otherwise returns pure dashboardMouseMsg Cmd. Fixture decoration calls original before incrementing produced inside returned Cmd. Cmd is executed asynchronously; typed delivery then checks frame and performs the single strict inspect.
actualPaths.alternatives: Callback not entered, original returned nil, Cmd not executed, Cmd not delivered, stale typed frame and inspect failure are distinct. Existing zero production/delivery cannot distinguish the first three.

recommendedGate.name: One original startup frame/output barrier before the first mouse; no elapsed-delay readiness heuristic.
steps: Require existing Init/grid/restored progress predicates, and record a bounded startup fingerprint from original mouseFrame, fully visible row0 region, expected selection/IDs and grid. Reject any startup fingerprint drift; use no model/viewport/selection assignment.

Require original emitted alternate-screen/cell-motion/SGR enable sequences AND initial roster content from the original renderer output, not merely capability-query bytes or progress revision. Keep exact source-derived token/byte ranges as diagnostics, never synthetic screen data.

For a positive original-write-success gate, propose a passive forwarding output observer in the test wrapper only. It returns original(n,err), forwards the identical bytes exactly once, and records monotonically numbered bounded output ranges/hashes plus full-write/return/error observations. Publish a matching startup-frame write receipt outside the PTY; add no output marker/terminal command. Parent must actually drain and hash-match that complete successful original frame-write range before sending the mouse.

Reload progress and require the same startup fingerprint/region after the output barrier, then send ONE original SGR press and save actual write count, bytes-through/prefix hash and action ordinal. No repeat if short/error/unknown; retain original failure. Keep original typed-delivery and semantic/cleanup gates.

Keep the existing min(session deadline,5s) bounded wait; no fixed sleep, more generous timeout, repeated click or manufactured input. If readiness cannot be observed within it, stop before the mouse with partial output/receipts intact.
recommendedGate.orderingArgument: The startup marker must be recognized as a real renderer frame, not Program query output. Original flush holds renderer.mu while the observed original frame write succeeds and until lastView is assigned. Once the parent has observed that original write, subsequent onMouse acquisition either waits for that same critical section or observes a committed view. With a stable startup fingerprint this closes the identified initial nil/stale-handler window without touching renderer internals. It does not guarantee parsing, Cmd success or glyph paint; those original outcomes remain separately required.
observerConstraints: Keep tea.WithInput(os.Stdin) unchanged; do not insert a reader that hides the terminal descriptor.

Preserve original output terminal detection/sizing by explicitly forwarding term.File Read/Close/Fd and Name to the same original file. Avoid embedding unobserved WriteString/ReadFrom fast paths; every output write stays byte-identical. No library/product/pin/renderer modification.

No extra observer goroutine, model calls, Cmd execution, synthetic message or framework/private-lock access. Small fixed observation storage and independent synchronization; do not hold an observer lock while invoking model/callback code.

Record bounded success/short/error outcomes; metadata-write failure must never change the original output Write result. Missing/failed metadata means unknown readiness and failure, not permission to proceed.

Limit proposed observer metadata to64KiB/grid plus an explicitly budgeted small parent action receipt, fixed counters/at most64 diagnostic records. No log-every-keystroke or unbounded trace. All metadata shares the existing16MiB cap.
Instrumentation can change scheduling. A future successful instrumented attempt would validate that new harness cut only; it cannot retroactively prove this failure was the proposed race.

Do not treat os.read chunk boundaries as frame/write boundaries. Match complete original write ranges/hashes across arbitrary PTY read chunks; uncertain startup-frame attribution fails review/readiness.
